body:
Feedback from Glen - some application may not want or need to send logs out.

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **16.4.3** | Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a preferably remote system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. | 2 | v5.0.be-7.3.5 |

comments.body: What else are you doing with logs?

Processing in the same machine.

This requirement is not modified since v4.0.3 and I think it requires work anyway:
* what is the precise security problem to solve with this?
* what means "securely transmitted"?
* what is "a remote system"?

I would say that the scope for ASVS is that the application produces the information into the logs (contain expected information) in expected format (no log injections), but what happens later with the logs, may be out of scope already.

Ok, this version came about based on #199 and 92a711eca8499c8b4144f5c13bb83540f2a0f127

The original focus seemed to be on storing logs in a separate secure location. Since then it has slightly evolved.

The OWASP Top Ten Proactive Controls [currently says](https://top10proactive.owasp.org/archive/2024/the-top-10/c9-security-logging-and-monitoring/#secure-logging-design):

"_Forward logs from distributed systems to a central, secure logging service. This will ensure log data cannot be lost if one node is compromised. This also allows for centralized or even automated monitoring._"

The OWASP Top 10 risks [specifies as a risk](https://owasp.org/Top10/A09_2021-Security_Logging_and_Monitoring_Failures/#description):

"_Logs are only stored locally._"


So it seems like storing logs locally would not be considered acceptable unless the storage is in some local but secure location that is on the other side of a [trust boundary](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/securityengineering/sdl/practices/secure-by-design) from the application.

This sounds like it is in scope because the application has to be capable of broadcasting the logs where they need to go.
So the problem to solve is - if the application is taken over, logs are not influenced. I think it should be clarified in the requirement.

So how about:

"_Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. The aim is to ensure that if the application is breached, the logs are not also compromised._"
I'll handle the PR, it requires tag changes.
